concepts.name: Big-O notation
concepts.gloss: Asymptotic upper bound on growth.

concepts.name: Polynomials
concepts.gloss: Sums of powers of a variable with coefficients.

concepts.name: Complex numbers
concepts.gloss: Numbers a+bi, including roots of unity.

concepts.name: Multitape Turing machine
concepts.gloss: Deterministic machine with a fixed finite alphabet and a fixed number of one-dimensional tapes; running time counts bit steps.

concepts.name: Schönhage–Strassen conjecture and prior bounds
concepts.gloss: Multiplication of n-bit integers was known in O(n log n log log n), then n log n 2^O(log* n), then O(n log n) (Harvey–van der Hoeven); Schönhage and Strassen conjectured n log n is optimal.

evidence.quote:
Sch\"onhage and Strassen proved in 1971 that two $n$-bit integers can
be multiplied in $O(n\log n\log\log n)$ time on a multitape Turing
machine

concepts.name: Convolution and the discrete Fourier transform
concepts.gloss: Convolution of coefficient lists is computed by transforming, multiplying pointwise, and inverse transforming with the normalized DFT.

evidence.quote: Each normalized Fourier transform above is a contraction

concepts.name: Radix-digit reduction of integer multiplication to convolution
concepts.gloss: Splitting integers into radix digits turns the product into a convolution of short integer coefficient lists, followed by carry propagation.

evidence.quote:
Splitting the inputs into radix digits reduces multiplication to
convolution of short integer coefficients.

concepts.name: Signed Kronecker packing
concepts.gloss: Packing polynomial coefficients, including negative ones, into one integer so that a single integer product yields the polynomial product.

evidence.quote: The reduction is a signed form of Kronecker substitution

concepts.name: Harvey–van der Hoeven O(n log n) multiplier as subroutine
concepts.gloss: The established O(N log N) fixed-tape integer multiplier, used as an ordinary subroutine on small inputs, not recursively.

evidence.quote:
Calls to the established $O(n\log n)$ multiplier are ordinary subroutine
calls; they do not invoke the improved theorem recursively.

concepts.name: Polynomial ring modulo y^r + 1
concepts.title: Polynomial ring modulo $y^r + 1$

symbols.name: ring variable
symbols.meaning: The formal variable of the polynomials, whose powers serve as roots of unity.

symbols.name: coefficient count
symbols.meaning: The number of complex coefficients of a polynomial record, a power of two.

concepts.gloss: Complex polynomials of degree < r with y^r = -1; powers of y act as roots of unity and multiplying by one is a signed cyclic shift of the coefficient list.

evidence.quote:
one coordinate
is stored as the coefficient list of a polynomial modulo $y^r+1$, with $r$ a power of two

concepts.name: Synthetic polynomial transforms
concepts.gloss: Nussbaumer-style Fourier transforms over the negacyclic ring where roots of unity are powers of y, so the work is address rearrangement, signed shifts and two-point butterflies.

evidence.quote:
These are the
synthetic polynomial transforms of Nussbaumer and Quandalle and
Nussbaumer

concepts.name: Coefficient twist to negacyclic convolution
concepts.gloss: Mapping x to ζy with ζ=e^{πi/r} turns cyclic convolution of length r into negacyclic ring convolution, multiplying coefficient k by ζ^k.

evidence.quote:
A phase twist changes the last cyclic coordinate into a polynomial
modulo $y^r+1$

concepts.name: Bluestein chirp identity
concepts.gloss: Rewrites a Fourier transform of arbitrary length as a convolution multiplied by chirp phases.

evidence.quote:
Bluestein's chirp identity converts the middle transform,
including its target permutation, into normalized cyclic convolution.

concepts.name: Chinese-remainder map to prime cyclic axes
concepts.gloss: Places the digit coefficient list on a product of distinct prime-length cyclic axes in a way preserving convolution.

evidence.quote:
the radix-digit coefficient list is placed on a product of
distinct prime cyclic axes by a Chinese-remainder map that preserves
convolution

concepts.name: Gaussian resampling
concepts.gloss: Harvey–van der Hoeven technique expressing a Fourier transform of coprime-length axes through a multidimensional power-of-two tensor transform, with source and target permutations.

evidence.quote:
Gaussian
resampling then expresses each source Fourier transform through a
power-of-two tensor transform.

concepts.name: Fixed-point Gaussian dyadic numerics
concepts.gloss: Numbers 2^{-p}(a+ib) in a disk, stored as two's-complement records; intermediate values are exact and a single truncation follows a contractive layer.

evidence.quote:
Intermediate values are exact Gaussian dyadics,
whose real and imaginary parts have power-of-two denominators.

concepts.name: Array order and elementary tape scans
concepts.gloss: Arrays stored in address order on tape; linear-time scans, pointwise operations and field updates.

evidence.quote: \section{The machine model and elementary streams}

concepts.name: Fixed linear network exchanging two banks with restored auxiliaries
concepts.gloss: A fixed network of linear gates on role wires that swaps two data banks with signs and restores every auxiliary value.

evidence.quote:
We construct two fixed linear networks that exchange two banks of values
while restoring every auxiliary value.

concepts.name: Three-element subset construction with nested subspaces
concepts.gloss: Gather/scatter on three-element subsets with intersection-count pairings, plus side wires, give nested subspace labels with total rank deficit s < Wm.

evidence.quote:
The construction uses
three-element subsets: gather and scatter create coefficients depending
on intersection size, and auxiliary wires cancel the unwanted
coefficients.

concepts.name: Frames and pointwise gates on arrays
concepts.gloss: Invertible linear operators D_v giving the stored representation of each wire array; pointwise gates commute with a common frame so intermediate frames cancel.

evidence.quote:
We call $D_v$ its frame: the stored
array is $D_vg$ when the logical array is $g$.

concepts.name: Recursive rank saving
concepts.gloss: Edge operators of rank a need a smaller calls; since the total s of calls satisfies s<Wm, parameter growth by m raises cost per volume by s/W<m, giving a power saving.

evidence.quote:
This strict inequality
is the source of the power saving.

concepts.name: Address shear and Bruhat factorization
concepts.gloss: Updating fields (H,D) to (H+D,D) over a residue ring and factoring matrices into triangular pieces that can be applied in tape order.

evidence.quote:
The required factorization
is the Bruhat factorization for arbitrary matrices, with coordinate order
reversed

concepts.name: Fast interchange of address chunks
concepts.title: Fast interchange of address chunks in time $O(Vu^\tau)$

symbols.name: stored bit volume
symbols.meaning: The number of stored bits in the array.

symbols.name: field width
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each interchanged address field.

symbols.name: saving exponent
symbols.meaning: A fixed constant less than 1 giving the power saving.

concepts.gloss: Interchanges two disjoint contiguous u-bit address fields of an array of volume V in O(V u^τ), τ<1, using XOR combinations that cancel to an exact permutation.

evidence.quote: Its cost is $O(Vu^\tau)$ for a fixed $\tau<1$.

concepts.name: Simultaneous butterfly layers
concepts.title: Simultaneous butterfly layers in time $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$

symbols.name: stored bit volume
symbols.meaning: The number of stored bits of the numerical array.

symbols.name: chunk count
symbols.meaning: The number of equal-width address chunks in which one bit position is selected.

concepts.gloss: Apply H_0(u,v)=((u+v)/2,(u-v)/2) coefficientwise on the same selected bit in each of d address chunks in O(V d^λ'), λ'<1, with phase frames and a single truncation.

evidence.quote:
the cost is $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ for a
fixed $\lambda'<1$

concepts.name: Synthetic transform tape layout
concepts.gloss: Layout of roots, butterflies and stored frequency order on tape so the parallel layers apply and the same frequency order persists through the pointwise product.

evidence.quote:
The two forward synthetic transforms
retain the same frequency order through their pointwise product

concepts.name: Exact normalized ring products
concepts.gloss: Pointwise product of ring elements by signed packing and the O(n log n) multiplier, returning rounded results.

evidence.quote: \begin{lemma}[Signed packing and normalized ring multiplication]

concepts.name: Resampling with permutations left in the transform
concepts.gloss: Keeps source and target coordinate permutations inside the transform identity so they cancel and avoid full sorts.

evidence.quote:
We retain both permutations in the transform formula and
compute that formula directly.

concepts.name: Precision and exact recovery
concepts.gloss: Removing normalizations, showing coefficient error is below 1/2, rounding and propagating carries to get the exact binary product.

evidence.quote:
proves that the recovered
coefficient error is strictly below $1/2$

concepts.name: Sub-n log n integer multiplication algorithm
concepts.title: Integer multiplication in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time

symbols.name: input length
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each multiplied integer.

symbols.name: saving exponent
symbols.meaning: The constant 2^{-182} giving the power saving in the log factor.

concepts.gloss: Deterministic multitape Turing machine multiplying n-bit integers in O(n (lg n)^{1-κ}), κ=2^{-182}, by reducing to convolution, resampling, chirps and synthetic transforms accelerated by fast address interchange and butterfly layers.

evidence.quote:
We give a deterministic algorithm that multiplies two $n$-bit integers
in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ worst-case time

concepts.name: Modular arithmetic and congruences
concepts.gloss: Arithmetic on integers taken modulo m, with a ≡ b (mod m) meaning m divides a-b.

concepts.name: Prime numbers and coprimality
concepts.gloss: Primes are integers greater than 1 with no proper divisors, and integers are coprime when their greatest common divisor is 1.

concepts.name: Floor and ceiling functions
concepts.gloss: The largest integer at most x, the smallest integer at least x, and rounding of reals to integers.

concepts.name: Binary representation of integers
concepts.gloss: Writing nonnegative integers in base 2 as bit strings, and signed integers in two's complement.

concepts.name: Hamming weight
concepts.gloss: The number of 1 bits in a binary string.

concepts.name: Logarithms and exponentials
concepts.gloss: Standard logarithm and exponential identities, with lg meaning log base 2.

concepts.name: Matrices and linear maps
concepts.gloss: Matrices as linear maps on vector spaces, with products, inverses, and standard basis vectors.

concepts.name: Rank, subspaces and orthogonal complements
concepts.gloss: Dimension of a subspace or of the image of a linear map, and the subspace of vectors orthogonal to a given one.

concepts.name: Linear algebra over the field F_2
concepts.gloss: Vectors and matrices with bit entries where addition is XOR, including the general linear group of invertible binary matrices.

concepts.name: Gaussian elimination
concepts.gloss: Reducing a matrix to triangular or identity form by elementary row operations, expressing invertible matrices as products of elementary ones.

concepts.name: Triangular and permutation matrices
concepts.gloss: Matrices that are zero on one side of the diagonal, and matrices that reorder coordinates.

concepts.name: Tensor (Kronecker) product of vectors and matrices
concepts.gloss: The product acting on multi-indexed arrays by applying maps independently along each index.

concepts.name: Gaussian integers
concepts.gloss: Complex numbers whose real and imaginary parts are integers.

concepts.name: Dyadic rationals
concepts.gloss: Rationals of the form a/2^k, representable with finitely many binary digits.

concepts.name: Complex modulus and norms
concepts.gloss: The size |a+bi| of a complex number and vector norms with the triangle inequality.

concepts.name: Euler's formula and complex exponentials
concepts.gloss: e^{iθ}=cosθ+i sinθ, so e^{2πi/n} is a primitive nth root of unity.

concepts.name: Abstract algebra basics: rings and fields
concepts.gloss: Sets with addition and multiplication satisfying the usual axioms, and polynomial quotient rings as examples.

concepts.name: Fast Fourier transform divide-and-conquer idea
concepts.gloss: Computing a length-2^k DFT in O(n log n) by recursively splitting into halves combined with two-point butterflies.

concepts.name: Binomial coefficients and counting
concepts.gloss: Counting subsets and arrangements, including three-element subsets of a set.

concepts.name: Recurrences and recursion analysis
concepts.gloss: Bounding the cost of recursive algorithms by solving recurrences and by induction.

concepts.name: Little-o, Theta and Omega asymptotics
concepts.gloss: Standard asymptotic comparison notations and arithmetic with polylog factors.

concepts.name: Sorting and permutation routing on tapes
concepts.gloss: Sorting n items in O(n log n) comparisons or steps, and applying a given permutation to an array.

concepts.name: Schoolbook and Karatsuba multiplication
concepts.gloss: The quadratic digit-by-digit multiplication algorithm and Karatsuba's divide-and-conquer improvement.

concepts.name: Finite-state machine and constant-size alphabet
concepts.gloss: A Turing machine's constant-size control and alphabet, so each step does bounded local work.

background.summary: The reader has finished an undergraduate computer science degree: asymptotic analysis, basic algorithms, discrete mathematics (modular arithmetic, primes, counting, induction), linear algebra over the reals and complex numbers including matrices, rank, invertibility, subspaces and inner products, and elementary Turing machines. They have seen the idea of the FFT and polynomial multiplication, but not Schönhage–Strassen-style multiplication, Nussbaumer transforms, Harvey–van der Hoeven techniques, or specialist tensor and finite-field matrix factorization material.
